bigpic.t: The S&P 500 jumped 4.7% to exit correction and the Nasdaq 6.5%, led by Nvidia's 31% surge on Huang's return.

bigpic.b: The Fed is still set to hike
bigpic.t: on 9 Dec, with futures pricing about 93% odds. Wednesday's PCE inflation report is the next test.
as Trump signalled more time for Iran talks and surplus forecasts grew, days before Sunday's OPEC+ meeting on 2027 output.

stories.h: S&P 500 exits correction with its biggest gain in over 18 months
stories.sum: The S&P 500 rose 4.74% to 7,237.90 on Monday, ending a seven-session losing streak and leaving correction territory. The Nasdaq gained 6.51% and the Dow 3.01%, or 1,448 points, while the VIX fell about 26% to 26.6. Gainers beat decliners roughly five to one on the NYSE.
stories.why: The rebound eases fears of a wider unwind, but inflation data and the 9 Dec Fed decision still hang over valuations.

stories.h: Holiday week: PCE inflation on Wednesday, markets shut Thursday
stories.sum: October PCE inflation, the second Q3 GDP estimate and durable goods orders all land Wednesday, with jobless claims brought forward a day. Economists expect headline PCE of 3.6% and core of 3.2%. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and shut at 1pm ET on Friday.
stories.why: Thin holiday trading can exaggerate moves after one of the most volatile stretches of the year.

stories.h: Nvidia soars 31% on Huang's return, its best day since 2003
stories.sum: Shares closed up 31.48% at $165.05 after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, 12 days after accepting his resignation. By mid-morning the move had added about $990B in market value, which 24/7 Wall St called the largest one-day dollar gain for any company.
stories.why: Restores confidence in the key AI chip supplier, though reported SEC scrutiny of its accounting is still unresolved.

stories.h: HPE beats on 50% revenue growth and raises its 2027 outlook
stories.sum: Fiscal Q4 revenue rose 50% to $14.5B, with cloud and AI up 69%, and adjusted EPS of $1.43 beat the $1.27 consensus. HPE guided fiscal 2027 revenue to $59.4B to $63.1B and EPS to $5.05 to $5.35. Shares slipped over 6% after hours following an 18% gain in the session.
stories.why: Shows AI server demand turning into revenue for hardware makers, though Monday's rally had priced in much of it.

stories.h: CrowdStrike falls 9% after agreeing to buy Zscaler for $43.9B
stories.sum: Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each, about a 34% premium to Friday's close. CrowdStrike closed down 8.9% on Monday while Zscaler rose 17.7%. The companies target $1B in run-rate synergies and expect the deal to close in the second half of 2027.
stories.why: A bet that customers will consolidate security vendors as AI-driven attacks multiply across endpoints, cloud and networks.

stories.h: Zoom beats estimates and starts paying a dividend
stories.sum: Fiscal Q3 revenue rose 4.9% to $1.29B and adjusted EPS was $1.59. Zoom declared its first quarterly dividend, $0.25 a share payable 17 Dec, and guided full-year revenue to about $5.1B.
stories.why: A dividend marks Zoom's shift from growth story to mature cash generator as revenue growth stays in single digits.

stories.h: Rally doesn't shift the Fed: odds of a 9 Dec hike stay above 90%
stories.sum: CME FedWatch showed a 93.2% chance of a 25bp increase on Monday, and Polymarket about 91%, down from 98% on 12 Nov. Bill Ackman warned on X that a hike would be a mistake that risks recession, arguing financial conditions have already tightened sharply.
stories.why: A hike lifts funding and deposit costs and squeezes borrowers just as credit markets are wobbling.

stories.h: Dollar climbs to a 19-month high on rate-hike bets
stories.sum: The US dollar index rose 0.25% to 104.07 on Monday, its highest in 19 months. The euro fell 0.74% to $1.0887, sterling 0.53% to $1.3017, and the yen weakened to 159.18 per dollar.
stories.why: A stronger dollar tightens conditions for overseas borrowers and pressures Asian currencies, including the ringgit.

stories.h: Bitcoin sits out the stock rally, stuck near $61,000
stories.sum: Bitcoin was up just 0.08% at about $61,213 on Monday evening as equities surged, and ether slipped to about $1,719. US spot bitcoin ETFs saw roughly $1.8B of net outflows last week, when bitcoin touched a two-year low near $55,000.
stories.why: Crypto is lagging the risk rebound, a sign that leveraged and ETF money has not returned yet.

stories.h: Payoneer gets conditional OCC approval for a stablecoin trust bank
stories.sum: The payments firm received preliminary conditional approval to set up PAYO Digital Bank, a national trust bank. If finally approved, it plans to issue PAYO-USD, a fully reserved stablecoin used as a balance inside Payoneer's network rather than listed on exchanges.
stories.why: Fintechs are using new US stablecoin rules to win bank charters and run cross-border settlement themselves.

stories.h: OCBC pilots stablecoin payments for cross-border business
stories.sum: Singapore's OCBC and StraitsX launched a pilot that lets business clients receive stablecoin payments that settle into their existing OCBC accounts. StraitsX handles onchain collection and compliance, and NTT Docomo Asia is the first participant.
stories.why: Shows Singapore banks folding regulated stablecoins into everyday trade payments.

stories.h: FDA approves AbbVie's Rinvoq as first systemic vitiligo treatment
stories.sum: The once-daily 15mg pill is cleared for adults and children 12 and older with nonsegmental vitiligo. In two Phase 3 trials, 25% and 23% of patients reached at least 75% facial repigmentation at week 48, against 6% and 7% on placebo.
stories.why: Gives dermatologists a first pill option for a common skin disease with few effective treatments.

stories.h: BridgeBio wins full approval for the first limb-girdle dystrophy drug
stories.sum: The FDA granted traditional approval to Welgemda, an oral drug for LGMD2I/R9, ahead of its 27 Nov target date. It is the first treatment for the condition, and BridgeBio also received a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.
stories.why: Full rather than accelerated approval lowers commercial risk, and the voucher is a saleable asset.

stories.h: Lilly buys LoQus23 for up to $725M to target Huntington's disease
stories.sum: Lilly acquired the Cambridge, UK, preclinical biotech for up to $725M in cash, including milestones. Its lead drug LQT-23 is an oral MSH3 inhibitor, with a clinical trial application expected by the end of 2026.
stories.why: Huntington's has no approved disease-modifying treatment, and big pharma keeps paying up for early neuroscience bets.

stories.h: Brent drops below $90 as Trump signals more time for Iran talks
stories.sum: Brent settled 3.5% lower at $89.37 and WTI fell 4.5% to $80.17 on Monday as traders unwound hedges against a weekend escalation. The IEA sees a surplus of about 2M barrels a day this quarter, even as tanker attacks near Hormuz continue.
stories.why: Cheaper crude eases inflation pressure, but attacks on Gulf shipping keep supply risk alive.

stories.h: OPEC+ meets Sunday to set 2027 output baselines
stories.sum: The 29 Nov ministerial meeting is expected to agree a 2027 framework based on a capacity review, since group-wide targets run only to 31 Dec. Seven core members have held combined output targets at 31.01M barrels a day.
stories.why: New baselines decide who can pump more next year as the market tips toward surplus.

stories.h: Dutch court bars BYD's Ti7 SUV from the EU over Defender likeness
stories.sum: A Hague judge's preliminary ruling on 20 Nov bans BYD from importing or selling the Ti7 in the EU, including via its Hungarian unit, with fines of €100,000 a day up to €10M. BYD will appeal. UK sales, due in January, are not affected.
stories.why: Design-rights suits are emerging as a new hurdle for Chinese carmakers expanding in Europe.

stories.h: Canada gives Stellantis 30 days to fix breaches over Brampton plant
stories.sum: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said Ottawa will declare Stellantis in default of a 2022 funding deal unless it corrects alleged breaches. Stellantis plans to sell the idled Brampton plant to Roshel by year-end and says it will return about US$17M of support.
stories.why: Tests how far governments can hold carmakers to investment pledges as North American production shifts.

stories.h: Ford, Honda, Stellantis and VW sue New Jersey over repair payments
stories.sum: The four carmakers filed suit on 20 Nov in federal court in Trenton against a 2025 state law that raises what they must pay dealers for warranty and recall work. They estimate it shifts about $375M a year to dealers.
stories.why: If the law stands, similar dealer-friendly rules elsewhere could raise carmakers' warranty bills.

stories.h: Best Buy, Dick's and Abercrombie test shoppers before Black Friday
stories.sum: Best Buy, Dick's Sporting Goods, Abercrombie & Fitch and Kohl's report on Tuesday, with Urban Outfitters after the close. Bets against the group are heavy: short interest is 30.1% of Kohl's float and 17.4% for Dick's.
stories.why: These are the last big reads on consumer health before the holiday weekend.

stories.h: Fewer Americans expected to shop over Thanksgiving weekend
stories.sum: The NRF and Prosper Insights expect 182.7 million shoppers over the holiday weekend, down more than 2%, as 60% had started buying by early November. About 82% say they are looking for ways to limit holiday spending.
stories.why: Earlier, more cautious shopping blunts the Black Friday spike that retailers rely on.

stories.h: US holiday sales forecast to top $1 trillion for the first time
stories.sum: The NRF expects November–December retail sales of $1.013T, up 4.2%. Bain sees Black Friday through Cyber Monday above $85B. Visa's 4.5% growth forecast works out to about 1.1% after inflation.
stories.why: Most headline growth is higher prices; real volume growth is thin.

stories.h: Disney hits a 52-week high while Netflix is down 36% this year
stories.sum: Disney has been lifted by parks, cruises and a 97% jump in streaming operating income. Netflix has fallen 36.2% in 2026 after cutting its ad revenue forecast by $300M and raising prices three times in under three years.
stories.why: Investors are favouring diversified media groups over pure-play streamers as subscription growth slows.

stories.h: Dozens of CBS News staff take Skydance buyouts
stories.sum: Producers, editors and operations staff from Evening News, 60 Minutes and CBS Mornings accepted buyouts from parent Skydance, with the London bureau hit hardest. No exact headcount was given.
stories.why: Post-merger cost cutting is now reaching news divisions as owners chase savings.

stories.h: Skydance merges Warner Bros. TV and Paramount TV studios
stories.sum: The combined studio keeps the Warner Bros. name, led by co-presidents Channing Dungey and Matt Thunell, a month after the Paramount–WBD merger closed. Subscribers have refiled a lawsuit challenging the roughly $110B deal.
stories.why: Consolidation leaves fewer buyers for content and fewer independent streamers.

stories.h: Aviation groups ask Congress for $30B+ to fix air traffic control
stories.sum: More than 60 groups, including Airlines for America, Boeing, Airbus and GE Aerospace, urged at least $30B for modernization. The letter follows a 13 Nov nationwide ground stop, blamed on a single router, that cancelled over 18,000 flights.
stories.why: Outdated air traffic systems now cost airlines directly and cap how fast traffic and aircraft demand can grow.

stories.h: Macron pledges €350M for French aeronautics research
stories.sum: Speaking at Airbus's Blagnac site near Toulouse, Macron committed the money to the CORAC aviation research council and promised simpler permitting for high-potential industrial zones.
stories.why: Europe is using state money to keep its aerospace supply chain competitive.

stories.h: Air Force opens a $16.1B propulsion contract to 58 firms
stories.sum: The 15-year contract vehicle, running to November 2041, names 58 vendors for advanced propulsion work. Each received $1,000 at the outset, and the service is not obliged to spend the full ceiling.
stories.why: Gives engine makers and suppliers a long-term channel for military propulsion orders.

stories.h: GE Aerospace's defense chief Amy Gowder to step down
stories.sum: Gowder, who has led the Defense & Systems unit since joining from Lockheed Martin in 2022, will leave in Q1 2027. Engineering VP Darin DiTommaso becomes interim CEO while GE searches internally and externally.
stories.why: A leadership gap at a key military engine supplier as large Pentagon propulsion programs are being awarded.

stories.h: US housing braces for a harsh winter as sales slump
stories.sum: Pending home sales were down nearly 17% from a year earlier in October, and MBA purchase applications ran 18% below last year in mid-November. Real REMAX expects 2027 existing-home sales to fall 5% to 10% and national prices 3% to 4%.
stories.why: With 30-year mortgage rates above 7% and a Fed hike coming, a quick recovery looks unlikely.

stories.h: Blackstone REIT buys 75% of AWS-leased data centers in $5B deal
stories.sum: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust, public since May, will take a 75.1% stake in 13 newly built data centers net leased to Amazon Web Services, valuing them at $5B. Data-center REIT Digital Realty rose 3% on Monday with the AI rebound.
stories.why: Data centers remain the strongest corner of commercial real estate as AI demand grows.

stories.h: US apartment deal volume dips 6.7% in the third quarter
stories.sum: Investors bought $44.5B of US apartment properties in Q3, down 6.7% from $47.7B a year earlier, according to Newmark.
stories.why: High borrowing costs are slowing the recovery in commercial property transactions.

stories.h: Singapore core inflation cools to 1.5% on cheaper electricity
stories.sum: Core inflation eased to 1.5% in October from 2.0%, and headline to 1.9%, as electricity and gas inflation fell from 8.7% to 1% after a lower tariff. MAS and MTI expect core to pick up in Q1 2027 and average 1.5% to 2.5% next year.
stories.why: Price pressure is easing for households, but officials see upside risks into early 2027.

stories.h: Singapore's final Q3 GDP and 2027 forecast due this morning
stories.sum: MTI releases its Q3 Economic Survey at 8am today. The advance estimate showed 5.4% growth from a year earlier. DBS expects a revision to 5.6% and a first 2027 forecast range of 2.5% to 4.5%.
stories.why: The 2027 forecast sets expectations for jobs, wages and MAS policy next year.

stories.h: KLCI slips 0.5% as utilities drag; ringgit eases to 4.12
stories.sum: The FBM KLCI fell 7.46 points to 1,549.05 on Monday, with Tenaga Nasional among the biggest drags and losers outnumbering gainers nearly three to one. The ringgit closed at 4.1205 per dollar from 4.1105 as investors braced for a hawkish Fed.
stories.why: A softer ringgit raises import costs and shows Fed-hike bets pulling money toward the dollar.

stories.h: S&P Global sees Malaysia's growth easing to 5.1% in 2027
stories.sum: The agency expects Malaysia to grow 5.5% this year and 5.1% next, with Asia-Pacific slowing to 4.4% from 4.8%. Separately, UOB Kay Hian expects Bank Negara to raise the OPR by 25bp to 3% in Q1 2027.
stories.why: Growth near 5% plus a possible OPR hike would mark a turn toward tighter policy in Malaysia.
